result.title: When Should Agents Think? Adaptive Reasoning via Cross-Turn Estimation
result.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks. They typically perform reasoning before each action throughout an interaction trajectory. However, reasoning may not be necessary at every turn, as reasoning produced earlier can continue to support subsequent actions. A key challenge is therefore to determine when existing reasoning remains sufficient and when a new reasoning step is needed, without relying on costly generation-based verification. We find that decreases in the likelihood of subsequent reference actions after removing additional reasoning closely track whether those actions remain recoverable given earlier reasoning, providing an effective and lightweight signal for estimating cross-turn action support. Based on this observation, we propose Reasoning Adaptation through Cross-Turn Estimation (RACE), a training approach for adaptive agent reasoning. RACE introduces a Likelihood-Guided Progressive Reasoning Cover Detection (LoGiC) procedure that progressively identifies reasoning turns whose removal has limited impact on the current and subsequent reference actions. The resulting removal signals are incorporated into both supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning, enabling the policy to learn when to reason and when to act directly. Extensive experiments on four representative agent benchmarks show that RACE substantially reduces reasoning cost while maintaining or improving task performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RACE，用移除某轮推理后参考动作似然的变化来估计跨轮次的动作支撑度，并通过 LoGiC 逐步找出影响较小的推理轮次，把该信号注入 SFT 与 agentic RL，使 LLM agent 学会何时推理、何时直接行动，在四个基准上降低推理成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「已有推理是否仍足以支撑后续动作」的跨轮似然估计与 THINK/STOP 决策、动态计算和停止判据直接相关，可能为判断 LVR 中 latent 推理状态是否需更新、以及构造「保留/移除推理」监督信号提供可供核查的线索；但工作在纯文本 agent 上验证，视觉与 latent 状态的有效性尚待核查。
